The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

function.name: get_url_content

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `nvidia-a6000` |
| **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230901` (or the latest 20.04 image) |
| **Machine type** – 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM (adjustable) | `n1-standard-8` |
| **Boot disk size** – 50 GB | `--boot-disk-size=50GB` |
| **GPU count** – 1 | `--accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1` |
| **GPU driver installation** – automatic via `--metadata` | `install-nvidia-driver=true` |
| **Project & Zone** – replace placeholders | `--project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --zone=us-central1-a` |

---

## 1. Prerequisites

1. **Enable the Compute Engine API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Enable the NVIDIA GPU driver installation** (optional but recommended)  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute instances add-metadata YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME \
     --metadata install-nvidia-driver=true
   ```

3. **Make sure you have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated**  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth login
   gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
   ```

4. **Choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 GPUs**  
   Currently, `us-central1-a`, `us-central1-b`, `us-central1-c`, `us-central1-f`, `europe-west4-a`, `europe-west4-b`, `europe-west4-c`, `asia-east1-a`, `asia-east1-b`, `asia-east1-c` support the A6000.  
   (Check the latest list: <https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus>)

---

## 2. One‑liner `gcloud` command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-focal \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `--zone` | Compute zone (must support A6000) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | GPU type & count |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` | Installs NVIDIA drivers automatically on first boot |
| `--tags` | Opens HTTP/HTTPS ports (optional) |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed) |

---

## 3. REST API (JSON) – for programmatic use

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), use the following POST request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20",
  "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-focal",
        "diskSizeGb": 50
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

**Notes**

- Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` and `us-central1-a` with your own values.
- Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token (`<YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>`) via the standard GCP authentication flow.
- The `install-nvidia-driver` metadata key triggers the automatic driver installation script on first boot.

---

## 4. Post‑Launch Checklist

| Task | Command / Action |
|------|------------------|
| **Verify GPU availability** | `nvidia-smi` (once SSHed into the instance) |
| **Check driver installation** | `cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log` |
| **Open firewall ports** | `gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-http-https --allow tcp:80,tcp:443 --target-tags http-server,https-server` |
| **Attach persistent disks** | `gcloud compute instances attach-disk ...` (if needed) |
| **Set up GPU monitoring** | Install `nvidia-dcgm` or use Cloud Monitoring dashboards |

---

## 5. Quick‑Start Script (Bash)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu20"

gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-focal \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform

echo "Instance $INSTANCE created. SSH with:"
echo "  gcloud compute ssh $INSTANCE --zone=$ZONE"
```

Save as `create-rtx-a6000.sh`, make it executable (`chmod +x create-rtx-a6000.sh`), and run it.

---

### Final Tips

- **GPU quotas**: Ensure your project has the necessary GPU quota for the RTX A6000 in the chosen zone. Request additional quota if needed.
- **Billing**: GPU instances incur higher costs. Monitor usage via the Cloud Console or `gcloud compute instances list --filter="name=$INSTANCE" --format="json"`.
- **Driver updates**: The automatic driver installer pulls the latest supported driver. If you need a specific driver version, set `install-nvidia-driver-version` metadata instead.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
